$reason: The reference's panel made a menu, the consumer's options projected into it by an `<ng-content>` carrying only what Angular takes as a projection's own: its `select` spelled `SELECT`, which the compiler reads in any case, `ngProjectAs`, and an inline template's `*ngIf`, which the template takes and the tree copies onto the projection. None of them is written for an element, so point 1 lets the projection through, and the option of the template's own is what stands where it may not. A reader that took `select` in its case alone, or refused `ngProjectAs` or the template's attribute, refused the projection on point 1.
